title.value: INPUT SPACE MODE CONNECTIVITY IN DEEP NEURAL NETWORKS
title.justification: The title of the paper is clearly mentioned at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: I NPUT S PACE M ODE C ONNECTIVITY IN D EEP N EURAL N ETWORKS

analysis.description: The paper explores the phenomenon of mode connectivity in the input space of deep neural networks, extending the concept from parameter space. The researchers provide theoretical and empirical evidence of this phenomenon and its implications for adversarial detection and interpretability of deep networks. The study reveals that inputs with similar predictions are generally mode connected, even in untrained models, and discusses its applications for adversarial detection and interpretability.

type.justification: The paper provides a theoretical extension of mode connectivity concepts from parameter space to input space in deep networks and discusses this within a geometric and theoretical framework, such as percolation theory.
type.quote: We present theoretical and empirical evidence of its presence in the input space of deep networks, thereby highlighting the broader nature of the phenomenon.

name.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on investigating deep neural network architectures and their behaviors, which places it firmly within the realm of Deep Learning.
name.quote: We extend the concept of loss landscape mode connectivity to the input space of deep neural networks.

name.justification: The paper discusses experiments and phenomena related to inputs (like images) in vision models, which are a part of Computer Vision.
name.quote: We observe that different input images with similar predictions are generally connected.

name.justification: The study examines adversarial examples and mode connectivity's potential for adversarial detection, which is a core concern in Adversarial Machine Learning.
name.quote: We observe fundamental differences in connectivity between loss-minimizing inputs across various setups (real vs. real images, real vs. adversarial attacks, synthetic images) that allow us to distinguish between them.

name.justification: The paper explores input space connectivity to understand and interpret the predictions of deep neural networks better.
name.quote: We exploit mode connectivity to obtain new insights about adversarial examples and demonstrate its potential for adversarial detection. Additionally, we discuss applications for the interpretability of deep networks.

name.justification: The paper explicitly mentions using GoogLeNet for their experiments related to input space mode connectivity.
name.quote: Sections 4.1, 4.2, and Appendix A use GoogLeNet(ImageNet).

is_contributed.justification: GoogLeNet is not introduced as a new model in this paper; it is used for experimental purposes.
is_contributed.quote: First, we show how the two modes can be connected through the optimization of the loss barrier. Second, we study and exploit the connectivity between adversarial attacks and natural images to create an algorithm for adversarial detection. Third, we show that the connectivity exists for untrained (randomly initialized) networks, which validates our theoretical result in Section 5.

is_executed.justification: The model is executed for experiments related to mode connectivity with inputs.
is_executed.quote: Sections 4.1, 4.2, and Appendix A use GoogLeNet(ImageNet).

is_compared.justification: The paper does not present a comparison of performance metrics or results of GoogLeNet against other models, but rather uses it to illustrate findings in mode connectivity.
is_compared.quote: Vision models trained for classification tasks provide an ideal setup to observe input space mode connectivity.

referenced_paper_title.justification: The paper references the original GoogLeNet using its primary publication title.
referenced_paper_title.quote: We used GoogLeNet (Inception v1) (Szegedy et al., 2014) that was pretrained on the ImageNet (Russakovsky et al., 2015) and is available from the PyTorch torchvision library (Paszke et al., 2019).

name.justification: The paper mentions using ResNet18 to exhibit input space mode connectivity.

is_contributed.justification: ResNet18 is a well-known existing model used for experiments in the paper, not contributed by it.
is_contributed.quote: Finally, we show that modes, represented by class-optimal inputs, are connected even in the case of untrained, randomly initialized models.

is_executed.justification: The model is executed for conducting experiments related to input space mode connectivity.

is_compared.justification: The paper does not compare ResNet18’s performance with other models but uses it to demonstrate mode connectivity.
is_compared.quote: We used cross-entropy loss for all experiments unless explicitly stated otherwise. Experiments have minimal compute requirements and were carried out on a regular PC (equipped with GTX 1650 4GB) or cloud services (T4 16GB).
